title: WPMS/1700/2010 of RAM SINGH @ RAMESHWAR Vs MAHABEER AND ORS

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No. 1700 of 2010 (M/S)
Ram Singh @ Rameshwar. ........Petitioner
 Versus
Mahabeer and others. .......Respondents
Mr. Lokendra Dobhal, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Niranjan Bhatt, Advocate for respondents.
Dated: April 17, 2013
Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.
 Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused
the record.
2. Briefly stated that petitioner instituted Suit No. 22
of 2002 'Ram Singh @ Rameshwar vs. Mahabeer and
others' in the Court of Civil Judge (Jr. Div.), Uttarkashi
for permanent injunction for restraining the respondents
not to stop the petitioner for right of way to go for
irrigation alongwith his family members through plot no.
58 to plot no. 125 for harvesting and also for a decree of `
980/- for damages and further a decree of ` 4440/- as
damages per year till the reconstruction of the canal.
Respondents filed their written statement with the
averment that Khasra No. 58 does not belong to the
petitioner and there is no right of way to go for harvesting
alongwith the bull. It was also stated in the written
statement that in the Khasra no. 125, there is no canal for
irrigation. The learned Civil Judge (Jr. Div.), Uttarkashi,
vide order dated 01.08.2005, decreed the suit and
restrained the respondents from interfering in the right of
way of the petitioner at plot no. 125 through plot no. 58
for harvesting. It was also directed that canal would be
reconstructed in the earlier position on the cost of
respondents. The suit was further decreed for ` 3,000/-

2
for damages. Against the said judgment and decree, an
Appeal No. 5 of 2005 was filed by the respondents and the
petitioner also filed cross-objection in the appeal. On
24.08.2009, the learned District Judge, Uttarkashi
dismissed the appeal of the respondents and affirmed the
judgment and decree dated 01.08.2005. However, the
learned District Judge allowed the cross-objection of the
petitioner and decreed the suit of the petitioner for the
damage of crop for a sum of ` 2,800/- for the year 2002
and further decreed the suit for damages @ ` 4,400/- per
year, till the canal is reopened. Against the judgment and
order of the learned District Judge as well as against the
judgment and decree passed by the Civil Judge (Jr. Div.),
Uttarkashi, the respondents filed Second Appeal No. 59 of
2009 before this Court. The Second Appeal was heard and
was dismissed summarily on 23.10.2009. In the
meantime, the petitioner filed Execution Case No. 2 of
2009 'Ram Singh @ Rameshwar vs. Mahabeer Singh and
others' in the Court of Civil Judge (Jr. Div.), Uttarkashi, in
which the respondent filed objection under Section 47
read with Section 151 C.P.C. The respondents also
deposited the decreetal amount of ` 39,081/- for
satisfaction of the decree in the Court of Civil Judge (Jr.
Div.), Uttarkashi. The Civil Judge, on 24.02.2010 rejected
the objection of the respondents, holding that the decree-holder is entitled for the payment of decreetal amount
deposited before the Court. Against the said order, the
respondents filed Civil Revision No. 2 of 2010 'Mahabeer
Singh and others vs. Ram Singh @ Rameshwar'. The
learned District Judge partly allowed the said revision on
20.08.2010 and modified the order passed by the Civil
Judge on 24.02.2010 in Execution Case No. 2 of 2009,
thereby holding that the decree-holder is entitled to get `

3
2,800/- as damages of the crop and ` 4,400/- per annum,
as damages from the date of judgment i.e. 24.08.2009 till
the date canal is reopened. Against the said order, instant
writ petition has been filed.
3. Submission of learned counsel for the petitioner is
that the learned District Judge erred in law by modifying
the order passed by the Executing Court. He submitted
that the decree passed by the learned District Judge in
Civil Appeal No. 5 of 2005 became final, as Second Appeal
No. 59 of 2009 filed by the respondents against the said
judgment was dismissed summarily on 28.10.2009.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that in his
cross-objection, the petitioner has prayed for the decree of
` 4,400/- per annum as mesne profit by way of damages
from the date of suit, till the date of execution of the
decree, thus cross-objection was allowed by the District
Judge on 24.08.2009 and the learned District Judge held
that the petitioner is entitled for ` 4,400/- per annum till
the canal is reopened. Learned counsel for the petitioner
submits that the Executing Court cannot travel beyond
the decree passed by the Court.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the
respondents submits that the judgment dated 24.08.2009
passed by the District Judge is, itself, contradictory, as on
one hand the learned District Judge affirmed the
judgment and decree passed in Suit No. 22 of 2002, but
on the other hand, he allowed the cross-objection and
granted damages @ ` 4,400/- per year till the opening of
the canal (Gool). He submitted that since the District
Judge has affirmed the judgment and decree passed in
Suit No. 22 of 2002, hence the order of damages @ `
4,400/- per year will be operative from the date of order,
only. This submission of learned counsel for the

4
respondents is incorrect, in view of the fact that against
the judgment and decree of the District Judge passed in
Civil Appeal No. 5 of 2005, the respondents filed Second
Appeal No. 59 of 2009 before this Court, which was
dismissed on 28.10.2009, thus the judgment and order
passed by the District Judge attained its finality. Learned
counsel for the respondents further submitted that since
in the judgment dated 24.08.2009 passed by the District
Judge, Uttarkashi, no date has been mentioned from
when the damages @ ` 4,400/- per year will be paid, till
the opening of the canal (Gool) by the respondents, hence
the decree will be operative from the date of order only.
He also submitted that the Execution Case No. 2 of 2009
was not legally maintainable. This argument of learned
counsel for the respondents is not acceptable, as the
District Judge, Uttarkashi, in his judgment, has simply
allowed the cross-objection of the petitioner, which was
for the decree of ` 4,400/- per annum as mesne profit by
way of damages till the canal is reopened. Therefore,
petitioner's contention is that damages @ ` 4,400/- per
annum is to be paid from the date of judgment. Had it
been the intention of the District Judge, he would have
mentioned in his order itself that the amount of ` 4,400/-
will be deposited from the date of judgment.
5. For the preceding reasons, the writ petition is
allowed. The impugned order dated 20.08.2010 passed by
the District Judge, Uttarkashi in Civil Revision No. 2 of
2010 is hereby quashed. No order as to costs.
6. All pending applications also stand disposed of.
 (V.K. Bist, J.)
 17.04.2013
